title: Log4Shell JNDI lookup
event: A logged string containing a JNDI expression makes Log4j2 fetch a remote class.
root_cause: Message lookup substitution was on by default and JNDI reached arbitrary protocols.
detection: Outbound LDAP, RMI or DNS from a Java service and a literal jndi: expression in logs.
fix: Upgrade to 2.17.1, or remove JndiLookup and set formatMsgNoLookups.

rule.title: JNDI expression in a log or config
rule.impact: The parser resolves a remote object during a log write.
rule.fix: Patch Log4j2 and block outbound LDAP/RMI from the app tier.

title: PaperCut setup bypass and Bl00dy ransomware
event: Unauthenticated access to the PaperCut setup wizard precedes remote command execution and ransomware.
root_cause: CVE-2023-27350 allowed the setup flow to be re-entered without authentication.
detection: SetupCompleted pages reachable again and cmd.exe or powershell children of the PaperCut service.
fix: Patch 20.1.7, 21.2.11 or 22.0.5 and restrict the admin port.

rule.title: PaperCut version in the affected range
rule.impact: An unauthenticated setup bypass is reachable.
rule.false_positive: A lab install kept at an old build on purpose.

title: Exposed MSSQL brute force to Bluesky ransomware
event: An internet exposed MSSQL server is brute forced, xp_cmdshell is enabled and ransomware follows.
root_cause: Weak SA password on a public 1433 listener and a powerful stored procedure left available.
detection: A burst of 4625 events from one address, then xp_cmdshell and shell children under sqlservr.exe.
fix: Strong password, restrict 1433, disable xp_cmdshell unless needed, alert on its use.

rule.title: xp_cmdshell use
rule.impact: The database can run operating system commands.
rule.fix: Disable the procedure or restrict who can call it.
rule.false_positive: A maintenance script that uses it on purpose.

title: Barracuda ESG command injection
event: CVE-2023-2868 in attachment parsing allows command injection, a perl webshell and data theft.
root_cause: Unsanitised fields in a tar attachment reached a shell.
detection: perl -e socket children of the mail scanner and unexpected outbound traffic from the appliance.
fix: Patch, rotate every credential on the appliance, replace appliances that were backdoored.

rule.title: Inline perl socket
rule.impact: An inline perl process can be a webshell.
rule.fix: Confirm the parent and the listening port, then patch the appliance.

title: Volt Typhoon living off the land
event: Valid accounts and built-in tools are used for long dwell time, including portproxy for tunnelling.
root_cause: Weak edge device hygiene and credential reuse, no malware needed.
detection: netsh portproxy rules, unusual wmic or nltest use, long quiet sessions.
fix: Patch edge devices, rotate credentials, baseline built-in tool use.

rule.title: netsh portproxy rule
rule.impact: Traffic can be tunnelled through the host.
rule.fix: Record the rule owner and remove it when the tunnel closes.
